summary.name: Keka
summary.one_liner: Keka is a macOS file archiver app for compressing, extracting and password-encrypting files and folders, with drag-and-drop from the Dock.
use_cases: Compress files and folders to save space on a Mac
Split large files so they fit email or server limits
Extract archives of many formats on macOS
Compress files by dragging them onto the Dock icon
summary.what_it_does: Keka compresses files and folders into archive formats including 7Z, ZIP, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, XZ, LZIP, DMG, ISO, BROTLI, ZSTD and others. It can extract a long list of formats, including RAR, ZIPX, EXE, CAB, MSI, APK and IPA. Users can set a password to create encrypted files, using AES-256 for 7z and Zip 2.0 legacy encryption for ZIP. Large archives can be split into pieces that expand back to the original file. Files can be compressed without opening the app by dragging them onto the Dock icon or the app window.
notable: Drag-and-drop compression from the Dock icon without opening the app
Downloadable older versions for Mac OS X 10.4 through 10.9
Available on the Mac App Store, or free to download from the website with optional tips
caveats: Buying through the Mac App Store supports development; the website version is otherwise the same
ZIP encryption uses the older Zip 2.0 legacy specification, which is weaker than AES-256
Setting itself as the default app requires a separate KekaExternalHelper download
